PullRequest.Title: agentHost: preserve the engine snapshot pairing ID namespace
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## What and why

Keep missing engine input/output pairing IDs missing, rather than replacing them with an unrelated SDK model-call ID.

The restricted router falls back from `properties.modelCallId` to the top-level `model_call_id` for every target event. Engine snapshots mint their own input/output pairing UUID, so that fallback can manufacture an invalid correlation key. This change excludes `engine.messages` and `engine.messages.length` from the fallback.

For example, an engine snapshot with no pairing UUID and SDK ID `sdk-call-A` previously acquired `modelCallId: sdk-call-A`. It now remains unpaired instead of presenting that unrelated ID as an engine pairing key. Other target events keep their existing fallback.

This complements #345609: `sdkSessionId` / `sdkAgentId` identify the conversation and child trajectory, while engine `modelCallId` pairs an individual model input/output. Conversation correlation remains available even when the engine pairing ID is missing.

## Scope

The change is limited to the restricted router and its regression tests. It does not change content collection, consent, destinations, SDK dependencies or downstream admission. The tests no longer depend on the earlier host-provided ownership proposal.

## How to test

```text
pnpm run test-node --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostGitHubTelemetryRouter.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostRestrictedTelemetry.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotGitHubTelemetryForwarder.test.ts
```

Result: **48 passed** using the same Node test runner directly after refreshing the six selected telemetry modules and one newly added test helper with the repository's `transpileFile` helper. Other compiled dependencies were reused; this was not a full client build/typecheck. The installed local SDK is older than current main; the changed router imports its notification type only, and the focused routing tests use synthetic notifications.

The real restricted sender tests capture serialized upload envelopes and verify independent engine pairs with different headers, preserved SDK conversation identity, and disabled/misclassified-event suppression. Prior synthetic loopback HTTP validation also exercised the router and sender, but predates this main merge. No customer content, production telemetry endpoint, or live CTS ingestion was used.

Scenarios.Scenario: Restricted engine snapshot telemetry (`engine.messages` and `engine.messages.length`) emitted during a Copilot model call
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The SDK telemetry callback launches `_routeGitHubTelemetry`; for a restricted target it resolves the account context, constructs properties, awaits `multiplexProperties`, then schedules the enabled telemetry sink(s). Context resolution and gzip, when needed, must finish before routing reaches the send call; the sender's network delivery is fire-and-forget and therefore off the callback's completion critical path. The changed `isEngineSnapshot` check is constant-time and removes only the fallback `modelCallId` property when the native pairing ID is absent.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve `/copilot_internal/user` account and telemetry policy on a cold token
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one coalesced discovery for concurrent calls sharing a token; subsequent events use the cached per-token entry until invalidation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same context resolution occurred before this PR for every restricted target route, backed by the same coalesced cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold discovery blocks routing of the event; warm lookup does not perform network I/O.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Copy properties, gzip always-compressed or oversized string values, chunk them, and JSON-serialize the envelope
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per source event before sinks; the multiplexed object is shared by both sinks. Cost scales with telemetry property bytes, especially `messagesJson`.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same full property multiplexing and envelope serialization occurred; pre-diff engine snapshots missing a pairing ID additionally carried the short SDK fallback ID.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Property multiplexing is awaited before sink dispatch; envelope serialization is synchronous in the send call. Removing one short fallback ID for engine snapshots slightly reduces, rather than increases, bytes and allocation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: POST one Application Insights envelope to the enhanced GitHub telemetry endpoint
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One POST per admitted enhanced-GH event; no retry. `engine.messages.length` may additionally use the separate internal sink.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Exactly the same POST count and scheduling occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The fetch is started after serialization but is fire-and-forget, so response latency does not block routing completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Queue an internal telemetry event through the OneDataSystem appender for internal users
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One internal appender log for each admitted `engine.messages.length` event for an internal user; none for `engine.messages`.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same internal event cardinality and appender path existed before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The appender call is synchronous enqueueing; transport/flush is managed by the existing appender and unchanged by the diff.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Work scales with the number of SDK engine snapshot notifications and the byte length of their telemetry properties. Effective sink cardinality remains one enhanced event per admitted snapshot, plus one internal event only for `engine.messages.length` when internal. The new comparison remains O(1) per event and does not scale with message contents.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: SDK notifications can invoke independent async routes concurrently. Same-token cold account discovery is coalesced by the per-token client promise; warm calls reuse it. Large-property gzip jobs and fire-and-forget telemetry POSTs may overlap across events, as before. There is one enhanced-GH send for an admitted `engine.messages` event and, for an internal opted-in user, one enhanced-GH plus one internal appender send for `engine.messages.length`; the diff does not alter this cardinality or concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Restricted telemetry context uses a per-token cached/coalesced entry: the first event can wait for discovery, concurrent cold requests share it, and warm events avoid discovery. The changed engine-name classification has no cache and does not change cache keys, misses, invalidation, or negative behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the complete changed production hunk and its transitive router, compressor, account cache, enhanced sender, and internal sender paths show unchanged expensive work and boundary cardinality.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual engine snapshot frequency and payload sizes vary by model call, but the diff neither increases event count nor payload processing; it omits one short property in the missing-pairing-ID case.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The PR adds two string comparisons per target event and suppresses one short property for two event kinds; it does not add serialization, compression, network calls, retention, or concurrency.

Scenarios.Scenario: Other allowlisted telemetry such as `conversation.repetition.detected` retaining the SDK model-call fallback
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The same SDK callback and cached context resolution lead to property construction, multiplexing, and the pre-existing sink. The new `isEngineSnapshot` comparison evaluates false, after which the existing `model_call_id` fallback and all downstream behavior remain unchanged.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve cold account context and POST the admitted enhanced telemetry envelope
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One coalesced discovery per cold token and one POST per admitted event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Both boundary calls and their cardinality are unchanged; these non-engine events still receive the same fallback property.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold discovery and property multiplexing precede dispatch; POST completion is off the critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Multiplex telemetry properties and serialize one envelope
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per admitted source event; cost scales with property bytes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No change beyond the constant-time engine-kind classification.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Multiplexing is awaited and JSON serialization occurs before fetch, exactly as before.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The only added cost is O(1) string comparison per allowlisted event, independent of payload size and collection cardinality.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Independent notifications can route concurrently; same-token cold discovery is coalesced, and each admitted event retains its existing single-sink cardinality. The diff adds no queue, limiter, fan-out, or serialization point.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Same per-token coalesced account-context cache as before; no cache behavior is changed by the event classification.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the false branch preserves the prior property spread and all downstream calls.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Notification frequency varies, but two primitive equality checks are not a realistic user-visible regression and do not amplify expensive downstream work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression; existing boundary and serialization costs are neither introduced nor amplified.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the full two-file diff and traced both engine and non-engine telemetry routes through account discovery, compression/chunking, serialization, enhanced telemetry POST, and internal appender dispatch. No diff-caused performance issue was found, and the PR is not evidenced as a performance-regression fix requiring blame attribution.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
